definition: Workspace is a bounded identity and lifecycle boundary for a working environment. It stores metadata and opaque resource references; it does not provide filesystem, terminal, process, credential, model, tool, MCP or runtime authority.
purpose: Give future callers one explicit workspace scope without making the workspace an execution engine.

identity.rule: Identity is explicit and stable. An unknown identity never resolves to another workspace.

kindRule: A kind is a declaration, not an authority. The provider must explicitly support a requested kind; the Workspace core never infers filesystem, process or remote capabilities from it.

metadata.rule: Metadata is descriptive and bounded. Authority-bearing keys, credentials, secrets, paths, commands, processes, runtimes and provider handles are refused.

resourceReferences.rule: References identify resources owned by another contract. Workspace never dereferences them and never stores their provider-specific location.

lifecycle.mountRule: workspace.mount performs the bounded logical transition created -> mounted -> active atomically. It does not mount a filesystem, start a process or bind a runtime.
lifecycle.releaseRule: workspace.release is terminal and idempotent after the first release. It releases Workspace bookkeeping only; provider resource cleanup belongs to an explicit future provider/executor contract.

operations.name: workspace.create
operations.rule: Creates one bounded identity in the provider namespace; duplicate identities are refused.

operations.name: workspace.describe
operations.output: Workspace record or null when the exact identity is not present
operations.rule: Reads only the exact requested identity. Null is an explicit absent result, never a fallback or cross-workspace lookup.

operations.name: workspace.mount
operations.rule: Advances only the logical lifecycle. It does not grant execution authority or call a runtime.

operations.name: workspace.release
operations.output: Workspace record in terminal lifecycle released
operations.rule: Makes the exact identity terminal. There is no reopen, delete, execute or cleanup authority in this contract.

permissionRule: Read is limited to exact identity description. Create covers bounded lifecycle mutations. There is deliberately no ai:workspace:execute permission in P2.15.

provider.replacement: Any provider may replace the default when it preserves the interface and explicit supports(kind) answer.
provider.semantics: Provider state is isolated by workspaceId. Provider implementation and durability are not part of the Workspace contract.

guarantees: unknown identities fail closed for mutations
provider capabilities are never inferred from identity or kind

persistence: The provider owns storage semantics. The default in-memory provider is process-local and makes no durability claim; Workspace does not select or configure persistence.

security.failClosed: Malformed identities, unsupported kinds, duplicate references, forbidden metadata and invalid lifecycle transitions are refused deterministically.
security.noAuthorityEscalation: Workspace metadata and references never grant permission, capability, process access or provider access.
security.secrets: Credential-shaped keys and values are not accepted by the bounded metadata surface.

ownership.aiSetReconciliation: The official Workspace LEGO extends this one core workspace domain; no ai-workspace duplicate exists.

compatibility.ui: The frontend consumes declared metadata on demand and does not redesign or replace stock n8n UI behavior.
compatibility.replaceability: A provider or future executor may replace the bounded implementation without changing ai.workspace@1.0.0.
